scenes.say: This is Capybara Onsen. More and more of its guests are not people. They are AI agents, booking a soak on someone else's behalf.
The onsen is about to ship an accessibility upgrade to its booking form. To a person, the new version looks exactly the same. Not one pixel is different.

data.heading: Two versions of the booking form

scenes.say: But an AI agent does not look at pixels. It reads the accessibility tree, and there the two versions could hardly be more different.

So what does the upgrade do to the AI guests? We expected it to help. Two small pilots disagreed, so before the real run we registered a different prediction: bookings will hold, and tokens will go up.

data.title: Does the upgrade help the AI guests, or hurt them?

data.heading: Registered before the run

scenes.say: Both versions sit behind one Flagsmith feature flag. A Flagsmith experiment splits the guests fifty-fifty and tracks four metrics.

data.heading: One flag. One experiment. Four metrics.

scenes.say: The guests are language models driving real browsers. Watch this one on the classic form. Its preferred time is sold out, and the only clue in the markup is a missing pointer cursor. It clicks, nothing happens, and it clicks again. This was the worst case we saw.

visual.who: AI guest on the classic form

scenes.say: On the accessible form, the same time is marked as disabled. The guest reads that, and goes straight to the next free slot.

visual.who: AI guest on the accessible form

scenes.say: A coding agent runs the experiment, using a skill we built on the Flagsmith command line. Before anything goes live, it checks that every event arrives and that every user still gets the control. Then it waits for a person to approve the start.

data.heading: An agent runs it. A person approves it.
An agent runs it. A person approves it.

scenes.say: Three hundred guests later, this is Flagsmith's analysis.

Correct bookings: 156 out of 156 on the classic form, and 144 out of 144 on the accessible one. No difference at all. But tokens per guest went up by almost fourteen percent, and that guardrail is breached.

data.heading: Flagsmith's analysis, with the skill's verdict

scenes.say: Why? A capable agent recovers from its mistakes, so the bookings come out right either way. On the classic form, 24 guests took a detour first. On the accessible form, none did. But the accessible page takes longer to read on every step, and the reading wins.

data.heading: Fewer mistakes, more reading

items.note: of 156 on classic and 144 on accessible. Most were one or two wasted actions.

items.label: Tokens per guest
items.note: 36,465 against 32,091. The guardrail was: no increase.

A longer page costs every guest, on every step.

scenes.say: So when the agent tries to ship, the skill refuses: a breached guardrail needs a person. A person saw the result and accepted the cost, because the upgrade is for people. Flagsmith rolled it out to everyone.

data.heading: The skill refuses. A person decides.
The skill refuses. A person decides.

scenes.say: The skill is small on purpose: about sixteen hundred tokens of instructions, and one fact per line of output. A fresh agent ran the whole job with it in fifteen tool calls.
